questions.q: According to the summary, what did the first US drug prohibitions really aim to do?
a: Suppress minorities and ease anxiety about a fast-changing society
Protect children from addiction and overdose at home
Reduce crime by locking up dealers and users
Follow a public health plan drafted by doctors
questions.why: The summary says the 1914 crackdown came amid anxiety about industrialization and was pushed as a way to suppress minorities.

questions.q: What did criminalizing drugs actually produce, according to the author?
a: A profitable illegal trade run by violent criminal networks
A steady fall in the number of people using drugs
Cheaper and safer drugs sold in pharmacies
Better treatment options paid for by the state
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that banning a product does not remove demand, so criminal networks took over distribution and grew rich.

questions.q: Why does Hari argue drug possession should be decriminalized?
a: So users can admit their habit and get help without fear of arrest
So the government can collect taxes on legal sales
Because drugs are harmless when used in moderation
Because police have no interest in enforcing the laws
questions.why: The summary says ending the fear of arrest would let addicts be honest and receive the support they need.

questions.q: What makes someone more likely to become addicted, according to the summary?
a: Childhood trauma, loneliness and a lack of human connection
A genetic weakness passed down through the family
Using a drug regularly after surgery or illness
Living in a country with strict drug laws
questions.why: Hari argues addiction depends on the substance and a susceptible person, and that susceptibility often comes from trauma or isolation.

questions.q: Why did violence increase around drug dealing, according to the summary?
a: Dealers could not call police, so they used fear to protect their trade
Addicts became more aggressive as prices rose
Police encouraged rival gangs to fight each other
The drugs themselves made users violent
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that gangs outside the law need a violent reputation to deter robbers, and new dealers replace the ones removed.
